title: Genotype × Environment, Replication and Stable Phenotype Selection

content.overview: A phenotype is produced by genotype operating within an environment and developmental context. Breeders seeking stable traits therefore need replication and, where relevant, multi-environment testing rather than selecting from one room, one season or one plant.

vocabulary.definition: A situation where relative genotype performance changes across environments.
Use of multiple biological units or repeated observations to estimate consistent effects and variability.
Consistency of a target trait or relative performance across relevant environments or repeated trials.

sections.title: Environment can reorder genotype performance
sections.body: Cannabis research increasingly documents genotype-specific responses to environmental factors. A genotype ranked highest in one condition may not rank highest elsewhere.

sections.title: Replication separates individuals from patterns
sections.body: Multiple plants per genotype and repeated trials help estimate whether an observation is repeatable rather than a one-plant event.

sections.title: Measurement must match the breeding goal
sections.body: If uniformity, yield, architecture or chemistry is the target, use standardized sampling and environmental records so differences can be interpreted rather than merely observed.

workedExamples: A line that performs exceptionally under one warm trial but poorly at standard temperature may be environment-specific rather than broadly superior.
If two rooms differ in PPFD and humidity, genotype comparisons across them require those environmental differences to be documented.
commonMistakes: Selecting stable lines from one plant.
Calling environmental plasticity genetic instability without replication.
Comparing chemistry from inconsistent tissues or maturity stages.
content.practicalApplication: Define a phenotype protocol with genotype replication, randomized or balanced placement, standardized sampling and recorded temperature, humidity, light, irrigation and maturity context.
content.summary: Stable breeding decisions require replicated phenotype evidence in the environments that matter to the breeding goal.
